overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation for the candidate-name omission or the complainant's identification, and declined to review the claim that actions were taken without formal votes. No remedy was ordered.

allegations.summary: Alleged the commission concealed the names of three individuals who had expressed interest in joining the commission during the candidate review discussion.
allegations.key_passage: The Commission could choose the level of detail devoted to the topic of “Conservation Commission Candidate Review” and did not violate the Law by omitting the candidates’ names from the discussion.

allegations.summary: Alleged the commission revealed the complainant's name during discussion of his own OML complaints while concealing candidate names, a selective disclosure of personal information.
allegations.key_passage: For the same reason, the Commission did not violate the Open Meeting Law by discussing the Open Meeting Law complaint in greater detail, including identifying the complainant.

allegations.summary: Alleged the commission took crucial actions without formal votes, relying on the claim that all actions must be voted on, including by roll call due to remote participation.
allegations.key_passage: Because the omission of a vote in these circumstances, even if true, would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law, we decline to review this allegation.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
